notes: Identity verified from title page: Racial Progress as Threat to the Status Hierarchy: Implications for Perceptions of Anti-White Bias; Clara L. Wilkins and Cheryl R. Kaiser; DOI 10.1177/0956797613508412; Psychological Science 2014, 25(2), 439–446, online 16 December 2013. Supplied canonical text contains the primary research article through references; no PDF was supplied. The reference year 2013 is consistent with online publication. The assigned trustworthiness and attractiveness interaction outcomes do not correspond to Study 2 as reported here: its critical regression predicts perceived anti-White bias. No trustworthiness/attractiveness target can be assigned from this locator. Study 2, printed p. 442: Step 1 SLB main effect b = 0.45, SE = 0.09, t(157) = 4.9, p < .001; condition-by-SLB interaction b = 0.49, SE = 0.18, t(156) = 2.66, p = .01; condition contrasts at high SLB b = 0.53, p = .02 and low SLB b = –0.34, p = .14; within-condition SLB slopes racial progress b = 0.67, SE = 0.12, t(156) = 5.51, p < .001 and control b = 0.18, SE = 0.14, t(156) = 1.31, p = .19. Candidate statistics are kept in notes only; no coefficient standardisation inferred. Candidate model participant N: 168 recruited − 8 excluded for random clicking = 160. This is a recruitment-minus-exclusion derivation, not a printed critical-model N or a sum of explicit mutually exclusive final groups. No condition-specific final counts are given on p. 442. No N is inferred from degrees of freedom. Because the row-specific critical test remains unresolved, this model-size candidate is retained for parent field-scope review only.
